answer: Adaptive Arrival-Rate Throttling assigns each new identity a token bucket whose refill rate starts near zero and rises only after sustained, jittered activity. A sparrow-like burst of registrations collapses the shared grove allowance, forcing genuine newcomers into a slow queue. Enforcement keys on inter-arrival variance per subnet and device fingerprint. An attacker must rent many IPs plus aged browser profiles and pace signups over days, raising cost per identity roughly 30-50x versus a scripted garden of instant accounts.
